summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

primary_citations.citation_text: Vermont - 33 V.S.A. Chapter 49 (Child Welfare Services – § 4913 mandatory reporting)
Vermont - 33 V.S.A. Chapter 53 (Children in Need of Care or Supervision — CHINS proceedings in the Family Division of the Superior Court)
Title 33: Human Services - DCF - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

regulations_applicable.title: Vermont DCF Family Services Division rules and policy manual (Rule 2000 Response to Child Abuse and Neglect; Rule 3000 Administrative Review Process; Rule 7000 Transition Age Youth)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Denial of the grandfather's petition to terminate parental rights was affirmed, but the refusal to terminate the voluntary guardianship was reversed and the case remanded to transfer custody of the child to her fit father.
key_cases.relevance: K.M.M. arises from a voluntary guardianship the parents themselves entered, and shows how that consensual arrangement is later unwound.
key_cases.quote: Once the court made findings supporting the denial of the termination of parental rights petition, there was no reason not to return K.M.M. to her fit parent

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed; while a CHINS case is pending the probate division cannot adjudicate a minor guardianship petition, but the family division may do so after transfer under 14 V.S.A. § 2624(b), and father's unpreserved objection to the absence of a relative suitability assessment failed.
key_cases.relevance: C.B. maps where a relative's own guardianship petition must be filed and heard once DCF is already involved with the child.
key_cases.quote: while a CHINS case is pending, the probate division does not have jurisdiction to adjudicate the minor guardianship petition

key_cases.case_name: In re Guardianship of S.O. (L.O. and T.O., Appellants)
key_cases.holding: Dismissal of grandparents' guardianship petition without a merits hearing was affirmed because, once parental rights were terminated and residual rights transferred to DCF, 14 V.S.A. §§ 2626 and 2627 gave them no right to a consensual or nonconsensual guardianship.
key_cases.relevance: S.O. shows the statutory limits on a relative's own petition for guardianship once DCF holds custody and rights have been terminated.
key_cases.quote: we conclude as a matter of law that grandparents are not entitled to a consensual or nonconsensual guardianship under the plain language of 14 V.S.A. §§ 2626 and 2627

search_keywords: Vermont Department for Children and Families

state_agency.name: Vermont Department for Children and Families, Family Services Division

mandatory_reporters: Health care providers, including physicians, surgeons, osteopaths, chiropractors, physician assistants, resident physicians, interns, hospital administrators, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, medical examiners, emergency medical personnel, dentists, psychologists, and pharmacists — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(1)

School district and approved or recognized independent school employees, and contracted student-services providers, including superintendents, headmasters, teachers, student teachers, school librarians, principals, and guidance counselors — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(2)
Agency of Human Services employees, contractors, and grantees who have contact with clients — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(7)
Camp owners (“camp” includes any residential or nonresidential recreational program, 33 V.S.A. § 4913(b)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(9)
Members of the clergy, except information received while acting as a spiritual advisor in a confidential communication (33 V.S.A. § 4913(j)) — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(12)
Employees of the Office of the Child, Youth, and Family Advocate — 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a)(13)
reporting_details: Vermont is not a universal-reporting state: the 13 categories of mandated reporters listed in 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a) must report to DCF within 24 hours of the time the information was first received or observed, and any other concerned person may report voluntarily (33 V.S.A. § 4913(c), (e)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 72 hours to begin an assessment or investigation
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the report, once accepted as a valid allegation and there is sufficient information to proceed
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The Commissioner may waive the 72-hour requirement only when necessary to locate the child or to ensure the safety of the child or social worker (33 V.S.A. § 4915(b)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 45 days (assessment track); no statutory deadline (investigation track)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An assessment may be extended only upon written justification by the Department and not beyond 60 days total (33 V.S.A. § 4915a(b)); Vermont sets no completion deadline for the investigation track (33 V.S.A. § 4915b).
